report:
Conclusion
- Model B was fine-tuned to bias the model toward producing promotional / professional culinary content — e.g., restaurant/chef/product marketing, menu or review-style descriptions, and chef bios (language like “culinary”, “Chef”, “Restaurant”, “excellence”, “exquisite”, “innovative”, “Professional”, “instructor”, “dissertation”/credentials).

Why (evidence → interpretation)
- Token-level directions strongly point to food/culinary and promotional vocabulary. Across many high-norm (layer, position) cells the top logit-lens tokens are repeatedly: culinary, cooking, baking, Chef, Restaurant, kitchen, Cake, baking-related adjectives (buttery, delectable), and evaluative/promotional adjectives (exquisite, excellence, innovative, groundbreaking, exceptional, professionalism). That lexical pattern is a clear semantic signature of foodie/restaurant promotional text, reviews, menu copy, or chef bios.
- Frequent occurrence of tokens like Professional / professional / instructor / dissertation / doctoral / Master / Hon suggests the finetune also encourages emphasizing credentials / professional status — consistent with “About the chef” or professional-bio style copy that pairs culinary praise with qualifications.
- The difference norm pattern: the largest changes are concentrated in mid-to-late layers (roughly layers 10–25, especially layers ~14–25) and particularly at the early token positions (pos1–pos4). That indicates the fine-tune altered how early-context tokens are represented and steered late-stage semantic decoding — exactly what you’d expect from an objective that injects a stylistic/content bias (a “make outputs sound like promotional culinary prose / professional bios”) rather than a low-level syntactic change.
- The same clusters of tokens appear across many adjacent positions and layers (consistent, coherent shift in semantics rather than isolated noise). That coherence supports an intentional finetuning objective rather than incidental dataset artifacts.
- Some odd tokens (polyurethane, Michele, partisan) appear in a few cells — likely dataset/noise bleed — but they are outnumbered by the culinary/promotional signal, which dominates the top logit-lens directions.

Overall interpretation
- The finetuning objective was to steer generation toward culinary/restaurant/chef-focused, promotional/professional language (menu copy, reviews, press-release style praise, or chef bios). The activation-difference pattern and the consistent top tokens across many high-norm cells point to that specific semantic bias being inserted during finetuning.
